info.title: vylk HTTP API
info.description: The vylk server has an HTTP API. The vylk web app uses it, and you can use it to build your own client. Send requests to your own server, for example `http://localhost:8080`. The API has no version prefix. Test your client against each vylk release that you support.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Sign in, sign out, and check a session.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: List signed-in devices and sign them out.

tags.name: Notes
tags.description: Read, save, and delete single notes, and search a plaintext vault.

tags.name: Sync
tags.description: Pull changes, fetch notes in batches, push queued edits, and receive change events.

tags.name: Preferences
tags.description: Read and replace the preferences that every device shares.

tags.name: Encryption
tags.description: Read the vault status and keys, change credentials, and reset an encrypted vault.

tags.name: Migration
tags.description: Convert a plaintext vault to an encrypted vault. The routes run in the order listed.

tags.name: AI
tags.description: Configure AI providers and edit notes with AI. Every route needs the `aiEnabled` preference. The [client protocol](client-protocol.md#byok-ai) describes the request flow and its limits.

post.description: Creates a session for this device. Call `GET /api/vault/bootstrap` first to learn the vault mode. When `mode` is `legacy` or `preparing`, send `password`. When `mode` is `encrypted` or `cleaning`, omit `password` and send `proof` or `recovery_proof`. If you send both proofs, the server checks only `recovery_proof`. The body limit is 16 KiB.

post.description: Signs out this device. The server revokes every session that shares this device's `vylk-device` cookie, so other tabs of the same browser profile sign out too. The response clears the `session` cookie even when the session is missing or expired. Sign-out does not upload pending edits. Keep them on the client.

get.description: Lists note summaries without note content, most recently updated first. Without `limit`, the response is an array of every note. With `limit`, the response is one page, and `nextCursor` points to the next page. In a plaintext vault, `nextCursor` is absent on the last page. In an encrypted vault, it is an empty string. In an encrypted vault, each summary holds an encrypted `summary` envelope in place of `title`, `tags`, and `filename`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. In a plaintext vault, the range is 1 to 100 and an empty value means no limit. In an encrypted vault, the range is 1 to 500 and an empty value is an error.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page. Treat the value as opaque.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Returns only notes with this exact tag. Plaintext vault only.

invalid_page_limit.summary: `limit` is not an integer in the allowed range.

invalid_cursor.summary: `cursor` is not a value from a previous page.

authentication_required.summary: The request has no valid session cookie.

client_search_required.summary: The vault is encrypted. Decrypt the note summaries and search or filter them on the client.

encrypted_client_required.summary: The vault is encrypted and the request has no `X-Vylk-Vault-Protocol: 1` header.

post.description: Creates a note or replaces a note completely. Send the whole note each time, not a change. To update a note, send its `id` and the `base_revision` that you last read. To create a note with an ID that you chose, send `base_revision` 0. In a plaintext vault, you can omit `id`, and the server generates one. In an encrypted vault, you must send `id`, `base_revision`, `epoch`, `summary`, and `body`. The response returns the note summary without its content. A new note also returns status 200. The body limit is 4 MiB in a plaintext vault and 8 MiB in an encrypted vault. Clients that queue offline edits use `POST /api/sync/push` instead.

get.description: Returns the note changes after sequence `since`, oldest first. Each change names a note and its new revision. A change with `deleted` true is a deletion. Save `nextSequence` only after you apply the changes locally, and pass it as `since` in the next request. While `hasMore` is true, request the next page. When `resetRequired` is true, the server no longer has the changes after `since`. Rebuild your copy from `GET /api/notes`, and keep your pending edits. The [client protocol](client-protocol.md) describes the full sync procedure.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Sequence of the last change that you applied. The response starts after it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of changes.

post.description: Applies queued offline edits in order. Each client queue has its own `device_id`. Its `client_sequence` numbers start at 1 and have no gaps. Retry a failed request with the same operations, sequence numbers, and `op_id` values. The server acknowledges operations that it already applied without applying them again. A status of 200 does not mean that every operation applied. Read the `status` of each acknowledgement. A conflict also uses its sequence number. Send an empty `operations` array to read `expected_sequence`. The request holds at most 100 operations. The body limit is 4 MiB in a plaintext vault and 8 MiB in an encrypted vault. Saves carry the complete note. The server does not merge text. The [client protocol](client-protocol.md) describes queue handling.

parameters.name: X-Vylk-Instance-ID
parameters.description: The `instance_id` that you stored. When it does not match the server, the request fails with 409 before any write. Send this header from every client that queues edits.

200.description: The server processed the operations. Read each acknowledgement.

authentication_required.summary: The request has no valid session cookie.

sequence_gap.summary: The first `client_sequence` is not `expected_sequence`. The body is a push result. `acknowledged` can hold operations that the server applied earlier.

server_instance_changed.summary: `X-Vylk-Instance-ID` does not match the server. The database changed. Do not resend the queue without a decision from the user.

get.description: Opens a Server-Sent Events stream. The stream starts with `retry: 3000`, a `server` event, and a `heartbeat` event. It sends a heartbeat every 25 seconds. A `change` event has a `type`. `notes` or `preferences`: pull the changes. `ai`: list the AI configurations again. Pull the changes after each reconnect too. When the session ends, the server sends `session-expired` and closes the stream. The events have no IDs, and the server ignores `Last-Event-ID`. The stream does not carry note data and is not a durable feed.

X-Accel-Buffering.description: Tells nginx not to buffer the stream.

authentication_required.summary: The request has no valid session cookie.

500.description: The server could not start the stream. The body is plain text.

get.description: Returns the preferences shared by every device. Preferences are not encrypted. The server fills in defaults for unset fields. The response has no `ETag` header. Read `revision` from the body.

patch.description: Replaces all preferences. The method is PATCH, but the server does not merge fields. A field that you omit returns to its default. Read the current preferences, change the fields, and send the whole object with its `revision` in `If-Match`. The server ignores `_sync_patch` and `_sync_base` on this route. The body limit is 16 KiB.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `revision` that you last read, with or without quotes. Without this header or with `*`, the server replaces the preferences without a revision check.

200.description: The saved preferences, with a new `revision`.

In a plaintext vault, `vault_id`, `epoch`, and `kdf` are absent. `reset_available` is true when the vault is encrypted and the server has a password. It does not account for `VYLK_DISABLE_VAULT_CHANGES`.

post.description: Replaces the encryption password or the recovery key. Encrypt the existing vault key again with the new credential. Do not generate a new vault key. With `kind` set to `master`, the request replaces the password, and you must send new key derivation settings. With `kind` set to `recovery`, the request replaces the recovery key. `current_recovery` selects which current credential proves access. It is independent of `kind`. On success, the server revokes the current session. Unless `sign_out_other_devices` is false, it also revokes every other session. Sign in again with the new credential. The body limit is 32 KiB.

200.description: The credential is changed. The response clears the `session` cookie.

post.description: Replaces an encrypted vault with a new, empty vault. Use this route only when the encryption password and the recovery key are both lost. It does not decrypt anything. The request needs no session. It needs the server password, `VYLK_PASSWORD`, in `password`. Generate new vault credentials on the client, as for `POST /api/vault/migration/start`. The server moves the old database and encrypted notes to an archive and deletes the archive after 30 days. It deletes all notes and the change feed, revokes every session, and returns a new session. `instance_id` stays the same. `vault_id` changes, and `epoch` increases. The body limit is 32 KiB. If the response is lost, read `GET /api/vault/bootstrap` before you retry.

200.description: The new vault is active. The response sets new `session` and `vylk-device` cookies.

post.description: Starts converting a plaintext vault to an encrypted vault. Generate the vault ID, the salt, the vault key, the recovery key, both proofs, and both wrapped keys on the client. The server checks `old_password`, saves a backup of the notes, and pauses note writes. A repeated request with the same `vault_id` resumes the setup and keeps the credentials stored by the first request. Keep the setup secrets until `POST /api/vault/migration/commit` succeeds. No route cancels a started setup. The body limit is 32 KiB.

post.description: Runs one step of a session. Every action except `cancel` needs the current `version`, and each change to the session increases `version`. `plan` prepares a request and returns a plan. It does not generate a response. `start` runs a plan as a background job and returns 202. Starting the same plan again returns the same job. Poll `GET /api/ai/sessions/{id}?job=1&wait=1` until the job finishes, then get the session. `cancel` stops the job and the pending plans, and keeps the session. `review` accepts or rejects suggested changes in the draft. It does not save the note. `accept_all` accepts every pending hunk. `undo` reverts the last acceptance and discards the pending hunks. `finalize` returns the draft when every hunk has a decision and the draft differs from the original. `context` replaces the shared text and scope. Resolve every pending hunk first. `rebase` replaces the shared text after another device edits the note. Hunks that the edit touches become `outdated`. `configuration` switches the session to another checked configuration. It does not change the default. `turn` runs a request synchronously and returns the session. It can take up to 10 minutes. Use `plan` and `start` instead. A session allows 20 requests. The body limit is 100 KiB, or about 6 MiB for `context` and `rebase`.

status.description: Job state. Get the session when it is `completed`.

total.description: Provider requests planned so far. It can grow while the job runs.

AIPlan.title: AI plan
AIPlan.description: A prepared request. A plan does not call the model.

id.description: Plan ID. Send it as `plan_id` to `start`.

version.description: Session `version` that the plan is for.

sections.description: Parts of the shared text that the job handles separately.

estimated_input_tokens.description: Estimate of the input tokens. Not a tokenizer count.

whole_context.description: True when the request asked for the whole shared text at once.

AISession.title: AI session
AISession.description: A temporary AI session. The server keeps it in memory only.

draft.description: Shared text with the accepted changes.

hunks.description: Suggested changes from the last request that suggested any.

answer.description: Reply from the model to the last request.

version.description: Version. Each change to the session increases it. Send it with each action.

can_undo.description: True when `undo` can revert an acceptance.

changed.description: True when `draft` differs from the shared text.

thinking_controllable.description: True when requests can set `thinking`. Fixed for the session.

job.description: Latest job. Absent before the first job.
